name: Shinka
classification_notes: A monospaced serif with unicase-influenced Latin proportions matched to Japanese ideogram widths, placing it in the serif category despite its technical, display-derived brief.
summary: A monospaced serif built from Japanese bullet-train information screens, with a true italic that bends hard to suggest speed.
description: Shinka takes its structure from the display typeface used on Japanese bullet-train information screens, forcing Latin letters into unicase proportions to match Japanese ideograms. The result is a monospaced serif with exaggerated ink traps and a sharply slanted italic. Six weights run from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic.
foundry_blurb: Aeiou Tools trace Shinka to a 2019 trip to Japan, where bullet-train information screens established the core of the typeface as a monospaced serif with unicase Latin letters, later taking liberties like exaggerated ink drops and a fast-leaning true italic.

name: Zetal
classification_notes: A grid-built geometric grotesque with expanded horizontal proportions and consistent vertical-to-horizontal metrics, sitting between European geometric precision and mid-century American industrial signage.
summary: A geometric grotesque built on a rigid grid, taking its solidity from mid-century American water-tank and cargo-container signage.
description: Zetal merges the typographic heritage of the Enschede foundry with mid-20th-century American industrial signage, run through a strict geometric grid. Expanded horizontal proportions and consistent metrics give it a mechanical, technical presence. It ships in eight weights across three widths, plus a variable font.
foundry_blurb: Aeiou Tools call Zetal a geometric grotesk inspired by the industrial modernism of signage on water tanks and cargo containers, built on a rigorous grid that prioritises geometric clarity and a solid, mechanical presence.

name: Andret
classification_notes: A workhorse grotesque with humanist detailing and low contrast, built for small-size legibility rather than display impact.
summary: A low-contrast workhorse grotesque with humanist detailing, built to hold up at small sizes.
description: Andret is a general-purpose grotesque merging humanist detailing with a low-contrast, rigid structure. Six weights from Thin to Black come with matching italics. First sketched in 2018 and refined over several years, it reads as a considered rather than a quick release.
foundry_blurb: Aeiou Tools describe Andret as a workhorse grotesque merging humanist details with a low-contrast appearance that works well at small sizes, developed over several years from first sketches in autumn 2018.
